questions.q: What three sources supply content for our dreams?
a: Recent events, childhood memories, and deeper desires
questions.why: The text lists recent real-life events, childhood memories, and deeper desires as the three sources.

questions.q: How does the mind 'condense' dream material?
a: It compresses many details into a brief scene
It expands a simple idea into a long story
It repeats the same image multiple times
questions.why: Condensing is described as turning a half‑page dream into many pages of interpretation.

questions.q: What childhood experience does the author link to adult flying dreams?
a: Parents tossing children into the air
questions.why: The author says being thrown into the air as a child creates the exhilaration behind later flying dreams.

questions.q: According to the text, why are obvious wish‑fulfillment dreams considered less useful?
a: They are common and reveal little insight
They are rare and hard to recall
questions.why: The author notes obvious wishes like sudden wealth are not special and offer little to learn.

questions.q: What role does 'displacement' play in dream structure?
a: It puts important issues into trivial symbols
questions.why: Displacement is defined as representing important matters with trivialities in dreams.
